compare.TRIM_TRAILING: Ignore trailing spaces and blank lines

form.addHint: The platform runs the code in the student's project and scores the cases that pass
form.addDone: This stage already has test points
form.lineName: Name of the test points item
form.linePoints: Points of the test points item
form.rule: Scaled to this item by the share of case points passed
form.remove: Remove the test points item and its cases
form.codeDirHint: Relative to the project root; empty means the root
form.compileCmdHint: Leave empty for languages that don't compile
form.casesSummary: {samples} of them samples, {points} case points in all
form.showHiddenNames: Show hidden cases' names to students (when off they see numbers like "Hidden case 1")
form.incomplete: Test points are incomplete: IO cases need a run command and cases; a test script needs test files, a run command and a test name on every scored row; grading commands need a command and the original of every protected file
form.selfTestHint: Students can run only the samples on their current code, unscored; leave empty to turn off

trial.title: Try with reference code
trial.hint: Runs the test points as they are filled in above; the task doesn't need saving first. The reference code goes in the project root; name the files as the run command does. The compute is charged to the owner of this space.

result.margin: Slowest case {slowest} ms, limit {limit} ms, {left} ms to spare
result.overLimit: Slowest case {slowest} ms, over the {limit} ms limit
result.firstDiff: Differs from the expected output from line {line}
result.scoreFailedTeacher: This run does not count as 0: read the program output below and set the test score by hand when grading.
result.scoreFailedStudent: This run does not count as 0; your teacher will score it by hand.
result.hiddenItems: {n} more points come from checks that are not shown

submit.title: Code to be judged
submit.suite: This stage has {n} test points ({samples} samples); your hand-in is judged automatically
submit.suiteLine: This stage has {n} test points ({samples} samples); the result counts toward "{name}", {points} points
submit.hint: The platform records this version when you hand in and judges it; later pushes don't change it. Changes not pushed yet aren't in it, so have Cheese push first.
submit.missing: The project's code can't be read right now. You can still hand in; this version won't be judged automatically and the teacher will score the tests by hand.
submit.suiteOther: This stage is judged by {kind}, automatically after you hand in
submit.suiteOtherLine: This stage is judged by {kind}; the result counts toward "{name}" ({points} points)

history.title: Judge result
history.waiting: The other {points} points wait for the teacher

review.restore: Back to the test points' score
review.adjustRange: The test score must be a whole number from 0 to {max}
review.reasonRequired: Write why the test score is adjusted
review.adjustedNote: The teacher adjusted the test score: {reason}

brief.title: Automatic judging
brief.summary: {n} test points, {samples} of them samples · {runtime} · {ms} ms and {mb} MB per case. When you hand in, the platform runs the code on your project's default branch.
brief.rule: Scored by the test points: the share of case points passed, scaled to this item
brief.summaryScript: Test script · {runtime} · {files} test files, {s} s in all. After you hand in, the platform runs the setter's tests next to your code.
brief.summaryCommand: Grading commands · {runtime} · {s} s in all. After you hand in, the platform runs the setter's grading commands in your code.
brief.protected: These files are restored to the starter originals before judging: {paths}

hint.IO: Feed each case an input and compare the output
hint.SCRIPT: Run your unit tests and score each test from the JUnit report
hint.COMMAND: Run your grading commands and read the score they give

script.limitation: Student code runs in the same process as the tests and can write wherever they can: this kind stops files that pretend to be a score, not deliberate forging at run time. Use input/output cases for exams.
script.filesHint: Copied into tests/ next to the student code before judging; yours win over a student file of the same name. Students never see them.
script.runHint: Write a JUnit XML report to $JUDGE_REPORT; the default fits the runtime
script.logLines: Output students may read when scoring fails
script.logLinesHint: First lines of the program output; 0 shows none (teachers always see the first 200)
script.averageHint: Each test in the report is worth 1 point, scaled to this item by the share passed.
script.perTestHint: Only the tests below count ({points} points in all); extra tests in the report score 0, and a listed test that did not run counts as failed.
script.name: Name of row {n}

command.limitation: Grading commands run in the same container as the student code: this stops a submitted score.json from pretending to be a score, not deliberate forging at run time. Use input/output cases for exams.
command.commandsHint: Run in order in the code directory; stops at the first that fails
command.sourceLineHint: The last line printed by the last command reads SCORE: 7/10 (decimals allowed).
command.sourceJsonHint: The grader writes score.json at the repository root with score and max; items may list each check (name, score, max), and those with visible false are shown to teachers only.
command.protectedHint: Starter files students may not change: before each judging your original overwrites the student copy. Type the path, then upload the original.
command.gradersHint: Grading programs and data only you have, placed at their paths before judging (the file name by default; add a directory if needed). Students never see them.

import.hint: Upload a zip of paired 1.in / 1.out files (.ans and input1.txt / output1.txt work too)
import.doneUnpaired: Imported {n} hidden cases, 10 points each; {skipped} unpaired files were left out
import.notZip: Cannot read this file: it must be a plain zip (not encrypted, not split)
import.empty: No paired case files in the zip: it needs two files with the same name, like 1.in and 1.out
import.tooLarge: "{file}" is over {kb} KB and cases must be within {kb} KB; nothing was imported
import.tooMany: The zip has {n} cases; with the {existing} already here that is over the limit of {max}; nothing was imported
import.notText: "{file}" is not UTF-8 text; nothing was imported

selfTest.title: Self-test the samples
selfTest.hint: Runs only the sample cases on the code your default branch points at now; unscored, and not a hand-in.
selfTest.pastDue: Past the deadline; self-tests are closed

rejudge.title: Re-judge every latest submission?
rejudge.body: Each participant's latest version is judged again against the current test points. Scores already graded stay; code already judged on this revision reuses its result at no extra cost.
rejudge.nothing: Nothing to re-judge: every latest version is already judged on this revision
